paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. The Pharisees and Sadducees could read a red sky like a pro, but Jesus says they couldn't read "the signs of the times" (Matthew 16:3). They had the forecast down and missed the One standing right in front of them. Knowing a lot isn't the same as seeing what God is doing.

Then the disciples get the leaven warning and think it's about lunch. I get it, because I'm a stamper who has stared at a cookie box and missed the point. Jesus reminds them of the loaves for the five thousand and the seven loaves for the four thousand (Matthew 16:9-10). He had already shown them He could provide, so they had nothing to worry about. Their little faith was busy with the bread while the real danger was teaching that sounded religious and led the wrong way.

So here's what I want you to take to the oven today. Leaven works quietly, and a little bit changes the whole batch, so what you let teach you matters. Check what you hear against the Word, and trust the One who has already shown He provides. Then you can spot the bad leaven and stop panicking about the bread. And when it takes a minute to understand, remember that Jesus kept teaching His disciples until they understood (Matthew 16:12).
